317030.title: Nonexistence of symmetric self-complementary 4-inflatable permutations at 64

literal_record.title: Nonexistence of symmetric self-complementary 4-inflatable permutations at 64
literal_record.statement: Let $4\pi\in\mathfrak{S}_{64}4$ be a permutation that is **4-inflatable**, meaning that it has the equal-pattern-count property required for the paper's 4-inflatable permutations. Say that its inverse is also its complement when $4\pi^{-1}=\bar{\pi}4$, where $4\bar{\pi}(j)=65-\pi(j)4$. **Nonexistence conjecture.** There is no 4-inflatable permutation on $64$ symbols whose inverse is also its complement. The authors' searches found no such permutation within the restricted class, despite extensive computation, so the claim remains a computationally motivated conjecture.
literal_record.source_name: Joshua Cooper and Andrew Petrarca, “Symmetric and Asymptotically Symmetric Permutations”, arXiv:0801.4181 (2008).
literal_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0801.4181

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2008). “In fact, $k=3$ was also resolved in the negative early on by Chung (). We conjecture that this pattern continues for all $k$.”

317030.primary_locations_read: 0801.4181 Conjecture 3, Proposition 11 and Lemma 12 context; Král–Pikhurko journal Theorem 3, Section 3 and Remark 8; Khovanova–Zhang Section 5 correction
317030.ordinary_attempts: Král–Pikhurko explicitly resolve CP Conjecture 3 in Remark 8. A 4-symmetric permuton is Lebesgue (Theorem 3); an inflated fixed permutation has density on its n diagonal permutation squares and zero on off-support squares, so cannot be Lebesgue for n>1. This covers n=64 without the inverse-complement restriction. CP pattern-count formulas are not a safe replacement definition: the 2021 paper corrects CP inflation calculations.
317030.precise_gap_or_exclusion: No new discovery; parity search or kernel proof of this known result receives no credit.

317236.title: The Genocchi descent pattern conjecture for packed words

literal_record.title: The Genocchi descent pattern conjecture for packed words
literal_record.statement:
Let $I$ and $J$ be compositions of $n$, and let $W”(I,J)$ be the set of packed words $w$ such that

$$
\operatorname{GC}(\operatorname{Std}(w))=I \qquad\text{and}\qquad \operatorname{ev}(w)=J.
$$

Here $\operatorname{totg}(w)$ denotes the number of occurrences of the patterns $21$-$1$ and $31$-$2$ in $w$. **The Genocchi descent pattern conjecture.**

$$
E_I^J(q)=\sum_{w\in W”(I,J)}q^{\operatorname{totg}(w)}.
$$

This conjecture proposes a pattern-counting interpretation of the generating function $E_I^J(q)$, whose specialization at $q=1$ counts packed words with the prescribed Genocchi composition and evaluation. The paper presents preliminary examples but does not establish the $q$-enumeration in general.
literal_record.source_name: Jean-Christophe Novelli, Jean-Yves Thibon and Lauren K. Williams, “Combinatorial Hopf algebras, noncommutative Hall-Littlewood functions, and permutation tableaux”, arXiv:0804.0995 (2009).
literal_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0804.0995

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2008).

317236.primary_locations_read: 0804.0995 Sections 2.1–2.2, 3.8 transition matrix, Conjectures 6.1–6.2 and printed five-word example; author-hosted manuscript appendix
317236.ordinary_attempts: Three ordinary routes examined: standardization converts the repeated-letter statistic to 31-2 with recoil refinement, but that is printed Conjecture 6.2, not its proof; deletion of the largest letter changes GC and adjacency across the deletion; a general Mahonian bijection does not preserve both GC and evaluation. See ORDINARY-ATTEMPTS.md.
317236.precise_gap_or_exclusion: Need a composition-refined weighted insertion recurrence matching the actual basis transition E, or an explicit coefficient discrepancy beyond the printed tables. No such recurrence or discrepancy established. Journal version/citing bodies incomplete.

317561.title: The least accumulation-point conjecture for permutation-class growth rates

literal_record.title: The least accumulation-point conjecture for permutation-class growth rates
literal_record.statement: Let $\xi\approx 2.30524$ be the unique positive root of $x^5-2x^4-x^2-x-1$, and let the accumulation points from above of a set of real numbers be limits approached by larger elements of that set. **Least accumulation-point conjecture.** The least accumulation point from above in the set of growth rates of permutation classes is $\xi$. The preceding proposition shows that the growth rates in $[\xi,\zeta]$, where $\zeta\approx 2.32331$, contain a perfect set and hence that $\xi$ is an accumulation point from above; the conjecture asserts that no smaller such accumulation point exists.
literal_record.source_name: Vincent Vatter, “Permutation classes of every growth rate above 2.48188”, arXiv:0807.2815 (2009).
literal_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0807.2815

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of July 2008). “These conjectures were disproved by Albert and Linton , who showed that the set of growth rates of permutation classes contains a perfect set (a set equal to its accumulation points, e.g., the middle thirds Cantor set).”

317561.primary_locations_read: 0807.2815 v1 Conjecture 4.5/v2 Conjecture 4.2; Pantone–Vatter 1605.04289 Theorem 8.3 and classification discussion
317561.ordinary_attempts: Pantone–Vatter give complete classification below xi and state the exact least-accumulation-from-above consequence. The original record reference to Albert–Linton refuting older conjectures is not a refutation of this particular xi assertion.
317561.precise_gap_or_exclusion: No new result. Classification proof dependencies, full tables and journal corrections not re-proved here.

317976.title: The nimber pattern conjecture for Sprouts on orientable surfaces

literal_record.title: The nimber pattern conjecture for Sprouts on orientable surfaces
literal_record.statement: Consider a Sprouts starting position with $n$ spots on an orientable compact surface, and let its nimber be the least excluded nonnegative integer among the nimbers of the positions reachable in one move. **Orientable-surface nimber conjecture.** The nimber is $0$ when $n$ is congruent to $0$, $1$, or $2$ modulo $6$, and is $1$ otherwise. The conjecture generalizes the earlier winning-player pattern and is supported in the paper by computations for starting positions with up to $14$ spots and orientable genus up to $9$; it remains unproved in the source.
literal_record.source_name: Julien Lemoine and Simon Viennot, “Sprouts game on compact surfaces”, arXiv:0812.0081 (2013).
literal_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.0081

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2008).

317976.primary_locations_read: 0812.0081 Conjecture 2 in v1/v2/v3; region/surface distinction and examples after conjecture; inherited r266 sibling 317975
317976.ordinary_attempts: A starting-position modular pattern does not supply induction over reachable positions. Source explicitly exhibits positions whose nimbers depend on genus. Splitting off a planar region requires a disjunctive-sum equivalence and exact mex classification, neither supplied by n mod 6.
317976.precise_gap_or_exclusion: No uniform classification of all reachable region states, no finite counterexample, no complete route. Source figures not visually reconstructed.

360924.title: Saturation spectrum conjecture for three unions of cycles

literal_record.title: Saturation spectrum conjecture for three unions of cycles
literal_record.statement:
Let $\text{ES}(n,3\mathcal{C}_{\ge 3})$ denote the set of edge counts of $n$-vertex $3\mathcal{C}_{\ge 3}$-saturated graphs. For $n\ge 14$, the conjectured spectrum is

**Saturation spectrum conjecture.**

$$
\text{ES}(n,3\mathcal{C}_{\ge 3})=([n+11,3n-11]\cup\{3n-9,3n-6,3n-5\})\cup\{n+1+4t:t\in[5,n-4]\}.
$$

The displayed intervals and additional values arise from constructions and previously established inclusions, but the equality is presented as a conjecture and is not resolved in the source.
literal_record.source_name: Yue Ma, “On the saturation spectrum of the unions of disjoint cycles”, arXiv:2311.16899 (2023).
literal_record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2007–2023). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1708.06076](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.06076), [arXiv:0704.0918](https://arxiv.org/abs/0704.0918).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.16899

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2023).

360924.primary_locations_read: 2311.16899 definitions, Observation 2.1, Lemma 2.2 proof, Theorem 2.3 construction equations, Observation 5.2 and Conjecture 5.3; 2025 publisher body denied
360924.ordinary_attempts: Join/core and block-gluing mechanisms sustained. K5 joined to an independent set has 5n-15 edges, precisely the printed S(n,5) endpoint; K2 joined to a cycle is printed W(n,2) with 3n-5 edges. K2 joined to an independent set is not saturated: adding an independent-part edge still forces every cycle through the two core vertices. K4 joined to one disjoint peripheral edge plus isolates also fails after adding an edge incident to that peripheral edge.
360924.precise_gap_or_exclusion: Need a nonprinted saturated graph with edge count outside the displayed union, including explicit proof of no three disjoint cycles and three disjoint cycles after EVERY nonedge, or full arbitrary-n classification. No such graph. Closed 2025 body and full citing literature unresolved.

379886.title: Cohomology conjecture for the complete graph \(K_5\)

literal_record.title: Cohomology conjecture for the complete graph \(K_5\)
literal_record.statement:
Let $K_5$ be the complete graph on five vertices. **Complete-graph $K_5$ conjecture.**

$$
H^{1,3m-2}_{{\mathcal A}_m}(K_5)=\begin{cases}\mathbb{Z}_2\oplus\mathbb{Z}^{5},&m=2;\\mathbb{Z}_2\oplus\mathbb{Z}_3^{4}\oplus\mathbb{Z}^{10},&m=3;\\mathbb{Z}_2^{5}\oplus\mathbb{Z}_m^{10}\oplus\mathbb{Z}^{10},&m=4;\\mathbb{Z}_2^{5}\oplus\mathbb{Z}_m^{10}\oplus\mathbb{Z}^{10},&m>4,\ m\text{ odd};\\mathbb{Z}_2^{10}\oplus\mathbb{Z}_m^{10}\oplus\mathbb{Z}^{10},&m>5,\ m\text{ even}.
\end{cases}
$$

The source presents this as a conjectural computational pattern and gives no resolution.
literal_record.source_name: Milena D. Pabiniak, Jozef H. Przytycki and Radmila Sazdanovic, “On the first group of the chromatic cohomology of graphs”, arXiv:math/0607326 (2006).
literal_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0607326

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2006). “This is still an open problem, and motivated by this we thought that for $\A_3$ graph homology torsion will be rather limited.”

379886.primary_locations_read: math/0607326 Definition 2.3, variant Remark 2.4, Sections 2.4 and 8.3, Conjecture 8.12; rendered page 35
379886.ordinary_attempts: Grading j=3m-2 makes C2 vanish for K5, hence H1=coker(d0). C1 basis: ten edges, four component exponents in [0,m-1] summing 3m-2, equivalently four deficits summing m-2. Rank C1=10*binomial(m+1,3). Relations come from five exponents summing 3m-2, merging a_u+a_v only when <m. This gives a specific ordinary presentation, not a completed Smith-form proof.
379886.precise_gap_or_exclusion: Need unimodular reductions valid for every m with the stated odd/even torsion and exceptional m=2,3,4, or a verified m>=10 discrepancy. Rational rank alone does not determine Z_m or Z_2 torsion. No matrices/SNF executed; later gluing papers/journal body not cleared.

379984.title: The q-tetrahedron action conjecture for classical-parameter graphs

literal_record.title: The q-tetrahedron action conjecture for classical-parameter graphs
literal_record.statement: Let $Gamma$ be a distance-regular graph with classical parameters $(D,b,\alpha,\beta)$, where $b\ne1$, and suppose $Gamma$ is not a dual polar graph. Let $T$ be its Terwilliger algebra, $Z(T)$ its center, and let $x_{01},x_{12},x_{23}$ denote the indicated generators of the $q$-tetrahedron algebra. **The $q$-tetrahedron action conjecture.** If $b=q^2$, then there exists a $boxtimes_q$-action on the standard module of $Gamma$ such that the adjacency matrix is a $Z(T)$-linear combination of $1,x_{01},x_{12}$, while the dual adjacency matrix is a $Z(T)$-linear combination of $1,x_{23}$. This proposes a natural quantum-algebra action for a specified class of distance-regular graphs, beyond the cases already covered by the paper's assumptions.
literal_record.source_name: Tatsuro Ito and Paul Terwilliger, “Distance-regular graphs and the q-tetrahedron algebra”, arXiv:math/0608694 (2006).
literal_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0608694

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2006).

379984.primary_locations_read: math/0608694 Conjecture 13.9, preceding Assumption 8.1 comparison and Conjecture 13.10
379984.ordinary_attempts: The conjecture weakens alpha=b-1 assumptions of the proved construction. Existing action cannot be reused without proving all q-tetrahedron relations on the additional modules and centrality of coefficients. A single graph action would be a parameter instance.
379984.precise_gap_or_exclusion: No full module classification or obstruction. No journal/citing proof clearance.

378270.title: The Dumont permutation enumeration conjecture for pattern 4132

literal_record.title: The Dumont permutation enumeration conjecture for pattern 4132
literal_record.statement:
Let $\frak D^2_{2n}(4132)$ denote the set of restricted Dumont permutations of the second kind of length $2n$ avoiding the pattern $4132$, and let $C_n$ be the $n$th Catalan number. The conjecture concerns the cardinality of this set.

**Enumeration conjecture.**

$$
|\frak D^2_{2n}(4132)|=C_n
$$

for $n\ge 0$.

The authors note that this would agree with the corresponding enumeration for $321$-avoiding restricted Dumont permutations. The statement was presented as unproved in the paper, although the supplied context reports that it was subsequently proved by Bóna and associated work.
literal_record.source_name: Alexander Burstein, “Restricted Dumont permutations”, arXiv:math/0402378 (2004).
literal_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0402378

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of February 2004); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

378270.primary_locations_read: math/0402378 4132 question; Burstein et al. Discrete Mathematics 306 (2006), Section 3.2 Theorem 3.4 and proof
378270.ordinary_attempts: Published Theorem 3.4 proves D2(4132)=D2(321) for all n and obtains the Catalan count. Proof chooses a minimal 321 occurrence, uses Dumont parity bounds to force adjacent first two entries and even third position, then counts too many small letters. Thus exact question already answered.
378270.precise_gap_or_exclusion: New formalization or retelling is excluded; this is a read journal theorem/proof, not the record automated solved label.

378610.title: The genus-2 extremal metric conjecture

literal_record.title: The genus-2 extremal metric conjecture
literal_record.statement:
Let $M$ be a surface of genus $2$, with Laplace eigenvalue $\lambda_1$ and area $\operatorname{Area}(M)$. The known upper bound in genus $2$ is

$$
\lambda_1\operatorname{Area}(M)\leq 16\pi.
$$

**The genus-2 extremal metric conjecture.** There exists a metric on a surface of genus $2$ that attains the upper bound

$$
\lambda_1\operatorname{Area}(M)=16\pi.
$$

The conjecture seeks sharpness of the genus-2 eigenvalue bound and is described as work in progress in the cited paper; the source gives no resolution.
literal_record.source_name: Dmitry Jakobson, Michael Levitin, Nikolai Nadirashvili and Iosif Polterovich, “Spectral problems with mixed Dirichlet-Neumann boundary conditions: isospectrality and beyond”, arXiv:math/0409154 (2004).
literal_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0409154

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2004).

378610.primary_locations_read: math/0409154 Conjecture 4.1.3 and Bolza candidate; Nayatani–Shoda 1704.06384 Main Theorem and proof setup; 2019 Numdam journal body obtained
378610.ordinary_attempts: Nayatani–Shoda prove lambda1=2 on an interval of genus-two branched sphere pullback metrics with area 8pi, so product 16pi. The original source expressly permits the singular candidate. This is known in that intended class.
378610.precise_gap_or_exclusion: Do not turn smooth-versus-conical wording into new credit: the later paper distinguishes sharpness among smooth metrics from attainment. Technical period-integral lemmas and complete journal proof not independently reconstructed.

377462.title: Conjecture on flow roots of 3-connected graphs

literal_record.title: Conjecture on flow roots of 3-connected graphs
literal_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a 3-connected graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges, and let $F(G,t)$ denote its flow polynomial. Let $\phi\approx1.749$ be the flow root of $K_5$ in $(1,2)$. **3-connected flow-root conjecture.**

$$
F(G,t)\text{ is non-zero with sign }(-1)^{m-n}\quad\text{for }t\in(1,\phi).
$$

If $G$ is not an Eulerian graph with $m-n$ odd, the same conclusion should hold for $t\in(1,2)$. This is the flow-polynomial analogue of the preceding conjecture for 3-connected chromatic graphs; the source gives no proof or resolution.
literal_record.source_name: Bill Jackson, “Zeros of Chromatic and Flow Polynomials of Graphs”, arXiv:math/0205047 (2002).
literal_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0205047

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2002). “Indeed it is an open problem to determine the supremum of the real chromatic roots of plane triangulations.”

377462.primary_locations_read: math/0205047 v1/v2 Conjecture 32(a),(b), preceding Eulerian sign discussion and cubic results
377462.ordinary_attempts: Deletion–contraction can generate exact flow polynomials, but no graph and rational test point with wrong sign is known here. Cubic graphs are already handled by the surrounding theorems; choosing K5 only meets the excluded interval endpoint phi, and Eulerian odd-cycle-rank graphs are expressly excluded from part (b).
377462.precise_gap_or_exclusion: Need explicit 3-connected graph and exact wrong-sign/root certificate strictly inside required interval, with all published graph constructions compared. Generic polynomial encoding is not a witness. No execution.

377673.title: Vertically symmetric nest distribution conjecture

literal_record.title: Vertically symmetric nest distribution conjecture
literal_record.statement:
Let $(a)_k=\Gamma(a+k)/\Gamma(a)$, let $G=G^{\rm V}_{2n}$ be the vertically symmetric fully packed loop grid, and let $P_G(k)$ denote the number of diagrams with $k$ nests. Define

$$
A^{\rm V}_{2n+1}=\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}(3j+2)\frac{(6j+3)!(2j+1)!}{(4j+2)!(4j+3)!}=1,3,26,646,\ldots.
$$

**Vertically symmetric nest distribution conjecture.** The nest distribution is

$$
P_G(k)=k\frac{4^{n+k}}{27^n}\frac{(1/2)_{n+k}}{(1/3)_{2n}}\frac{(3n+1)!(2n-k-1)!}{n!(n-k)!(2n+k+1)!}A^{\rm V}_{2n+1}.
$$

Here $A^{\rm V}_{2n+1}$ is the number of vertically symmetric $(2n+1)\times(2n+1)$ ASMs. The conjecture was checked for $n$ up to $8$, but remains unresolved in the supplied text.
literal_record.source_name: Jan de Gier, “Loops, matchings and alternating-sign matrices”, arXiv:math/0211285 (2003).
literal_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0211285

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2002). “Conjectured enumerations of symmetry classes were given by Robbins , many of which were subsequently proved by Kuperberg .”

377673.primary_locations_read: math/0211285 Conjecture 3, product formula, printed checks through n=8, conditional Corollary 1 and hypergeometric summation context
377673.ordinary_attempts: Summing the proposed distribution by hypergeometric identities proves consistency of a formula, not equality with actual nest counts. Kuperberg ASM totals and the record solved-reference concern broader enumeration results and do not by themselves resolve this refinement.
377673.precise_gap_or_exclusion: Need an exact nest-refined recurrence/bijection on the vertical grid, or a source-new finite discrepancy. No enumeration performed and later qKZ/refinement proofs not cleared.

376552.title: Norm formula conjecture for odd XXZ ground states

literal_record.title: Norm formula conjecture for odd XXZ ground states
literal_record.statement:
Let $N=2n+1$ be odd, let ${\mathcal N}_n$ denote the norm of the ground state, and normalize the state by $\psi_{0\ldots 01\ldots 1}=1$. Let

$$
A_n=\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}\frac{(3j+1)!}{(n+j)!}.
$$

**Norm formula conjecture.** The norm is

$$
{\mathcal N}_n=\frac{\sqrt{3^n}}{2^n}\,\frac{2\cdot5\cdots(3n-1)}{1\cdot3\cdots(2n-1)}\,A_n.
$$

The formula agrees with the computed values for odd $N\leq17$ and is presented as one of the paper's conjectures; no general proof is given here.
literal_record.source_name: A. V. Razumov and Yu. G. Stroganov, “Spin chains and combinatorics”, arXiv:cond-mat/0012141 (2000).
literal_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0012141

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2000).

376552.primary_locations_read: cond-mat/0012141 Conjecture 3 in all three versions; Hamiltonian and normalization; later sum-rule literature routing only
376552.ordinary_attempts: Finite N<=17 checks are printed. A total-component sum rule is not a norm identity without an additional identity for squared components under the precise normalization. The two spin sectors and twisted even chain cannot silently replace the odd periodic source state.
376552.precise_gap_or_exclusion: Need exact eigenvector normalization and norm derivation for all odd N, or an exact source-new failure. Later complete proof bodies not read; no status-as-open claim.

318757.title: Song's q=t Schröder identity conjecture

literal_record.title: Song's q=t Schröder identity conjecture
literal_record.statement:
Let $(a;q)_n=(1-a)(1-aq)\dots(1-aq^{n-1})$ and let $\left[\begin{smallmatrix}n\\k\end{smallmatrix}\right]=(q;q)_n/((q;q)_k(q;q)_{n-k})$. Let $S_{n,i}$ be the set of permutations of $n$ letters whose longest increasing subsequence has length $i$. Define

$$
F_{n,k}:=\sum_{i=1}^k\sum_{\substack{a_1+\dots+a_k=n\\a_i>0}}q^{\sum_{i=1}^k\binom{a_i}{2}}t^{\sum_{i=1}^{k-1}(k-i)a_i}\frac{1}{(t^k;q)_{a_1}(q,q)_{a_k}}\prod_{i=1}^{k-1}\left[\begin{smallmatrix}a_i+a_{i+1}-1\\a_i\end{smallmatrix}\right]\frac{1}{(t^{k-i};q)_{a_i+a_{i+1}}}(q;q)_n(t;t)_n
$$

and, writing $\operatorname{maj}$ for the major index, define

$$
H_{n,k}(q,t):=\sum_{i=1}^k\sum_{\sigma\in S_{n,i}}q^{\operatorname{maj}(\sigma)}t^{\binom n2-\operatorname{maj}(\sigma^{-1})}.
$$

**Song's conjecture.** For the $q=t$ specialization,

$$
F_{n,k}(q,q)=H_{n,k}(q,q).
$$

The identity is the limiting $q,t$-Schröder identity studied by Song and Haglund. The case $k=1$ is immediate, with both sides equal to $q^{\binom n2}$; the source states that the conjecture remains for $k>1$, while this paper proves it combinatorially.
literal_record.source_name: William J. Keith, “Proof of a conjectured q,t-Schröder identity”, arXiv:0907.2991 (2010).
literal_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0907.2991

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of July 2009); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

318757.primary_locations_read: 0907.2991 v1/v2 Conjecture 1, Conjecture 2, Theorem 1 bijection and concluding generalization discussion
318757.ordinary_attempts: Keith proves full k=2, not all k. The paper explicitly leaves k>2 generalization as a goal; author homepage confirms that scope. Extending the Catalan-half-word correspondence needs multi-column descent/major-index control, not just the ordinary RSK bijection. Literal displayed F formula also needs index reconciliation with Song primary definition before using it computationally.
318757.precise_gap_or_exclusion: Need exact all-k identity in correctly sourced notation and a statistic-preserving multicolumn map. No claim that the title or abstract settles the MathDB record.

376256.title: Aouchiche–Hansen–Zheng conjecture on the Randić index and matching number

literal_record.title: Aouchiche–Hansen–Zheng conjecture on the Randić index and matching number
literal_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph on $n$ vertices, where $n\ge 3$. Write $R(G)=\sum_{uv\in E(G)}(d(u)d(v))^{-1/2}$ for its Randić index and let $\alpha'(G)$ denote its matching number. Define

$$
p=\left\lfloor\frac{n+4}{7}\right\rfloor,\qquad q=\left\lfloor\frac{6n+2}{7}\right\rfloor.
$$

**Aouchiche–Hansen–Zheng conjecture.** One has

$$
R(G)-\alpha'(G)\le\sqrt{\left\lfloor\frac{n+4}{7}\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{6n+2}{7}\right\rfloor}-\left\lfloor\frac{n+4}{7}\right\rfloor,
$$

with equality if and only if $G=K_{p,q}$.

The conjecture proposes the extremal connected graph for the difference between the Randić index and matching number. It was disproved by the existence of a counterexample; the corresponding restricted extremal problem for subcubic graphs was solved by Du, Hu, and collaborators.
literal_record.source_name: Pei Liu, Feiyu Nan, Suil O and Ruiling Zheng, “A sharp Randić bound for König–Egerváry graphs and a conjecture of Aouchiche, Hansen, and Zheng”, arXiv:2607.23918 (2026).
literal_record.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2009–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1607.08258](https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.08258), [arXiv:1104.0426](https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.0426), [arXiv:0906.5230](https://arxiv.org/abs/0906.5230).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23918

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of July 2026). “The analogous extremal problem restricted to subcubic graphs was recently solved by Du, Hu, and three of the present authors , where the existence of a counterexample to Conjecture was first announced.”

376256.primary_locations_read: 2607.23918 v1/v2 Conjecture 1.2, Section 3.2 Pell/complete-bipartite comparison and concluding counterexample paragraph
376256.ordinary_attempts: Source supplies complete-bipartite counterexamples to the conjectured floor extremizer, via maximizing sqrt(s(n-s))-s and a Pell construction. Both versions include the strict comparison. The literal record also says disproved.
376256.precise_gap_or_exclusion: No new witness or priority. Other three source-family papers and every journal proof not read; unnecessary to rebrand the existing refutation.

379844.title: Conjecture on nonseparating cycle types in nonorientable triangulations

literal_record.title: Conjecture on nonseparating cycle types in nonorientable triangulations
literal_record.statement:
Let $N_g$ denote the nonorientable surface of Euler genus $g$. A nonseparating cycle is **one-sided** when its neighborhood is a Möbius band, **two-sided** otherwise; it is **orientable-leaving** when deleting it leaves an orientable surface, and **nonorientable-leaving** otherwise.

**Conjecture on nonseparating cycle types.** If $g \geq 3$ is odd, every triangulation of $N_g$ has a nonseparating cycle that is one-sided and orientable-leaving, one that is one-sided and nonorientable-leaving, and one that is two-sided and nonorientable-leaving. If $g \geq 4$ is even, every triangulation of $N_g$ has a nonseparating cycle that is one-sided and nonorientable-leaving, one that is two-sided and orientable-leaving, and one that is two-sided and nonorientable-leaving.

The assertion extends the verified low-genus pattern for $N_1$, $N_2$, $N_3$, and $N_4$. No proof or counterexample is supplied for the stated general ranges.
literal_record.source_name: Thom Sulanke, “Irreducible triangulations of low genus surfaces”, arXiv:math/0606690 (2006).
literal_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0606690

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2006).

379844.primary_locations_read: math/0606690 Theorem 3 and Conjecture 2; irreducible-triangulation discussion
379844.ordinary_attempts: Checking irreducibles in N1–N4 is already printed. Contracting edges preserves some cycle types but no argument lifts all required one/two-sided and orientability-of-complement types through every contraction in all genera. Abstract surface topology does not ensure a simple cycle exists in the given 1-skeleton in the requested class.
379844.precise_gap_or_exclusion: Need uniform irreducible-triangulation theorem or an explicit embedding certificate and exhaustive cycle obstruction. No concrete embedding, no visual figure audit, no complete source-eligibility clearance.

321114.title: Bonnington–Watkins conjecture on infinite face-boundaries

literal_record.title: Bonnington–Watkins conjecture on infinite face-boundaries
literal_record.statement: Let $G$ be a locally finite vertex-transitive graph of connectivity $3$, and consider a planar embedding of $G$. **Bonnington–Watkins conjecture.** No such embedding has a vertex incident with more than one infinite face-boundary. 360521.title: Havet–Thomassé conjecture for trees with few leaves

literal_record.title: Havet–Thomassé conjecture for trees with few leaves
literal_record.statement: Let $T$ be an oriented tree with $k$ edges and $ll$ leaves, and let a tournament be an orientation of a complete graph. **Havet–Thomassé's conjecture.** Every tournament on $k+\ell$ vertices contains a copy of $T$. The bound is motivated by the sharper behavior of paths and trees with few leaves; later results give near-linear bounds, but the stated bound is not known in general.
literal_record.source_name: Maya Stein, “Oriented trees and paths in digraphs”, arXiv:2310.18719 (2024).
literal_record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2010–2023). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1912.04004](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.04004), [arXiv:1010.4429](https://arxiv.org/abs/1010.4429).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.18719

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).

360521.ordinary_attempts: Known k+C*l and sufficiently-large-k-for-fixed-l bounds leave exact coefficient one and all small parameter pairs unpaid. Leaf deletion would require an unused tournament vertex with the required direction at the embedded parent; a bare embedding induction does not guarantee this.
360521.precise_gap_or_exclusion: No all-orientation tree embedding route or finite tournament obstruction. Companion 1912.04004/1010.4429 proofs not fully read.

318554.title: The linear t-pebbling bound conjecture

literal_record.title: The linear t-pebbling bound conjecture
literal_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $t\geq 1$, and let $\operatorname{diam}(G)$ denote its diameter.

**Linear t-pebbling bound conjecture.**

$$
\pi_t(G) \leq \pi(G) + 2^{\operatorname{diam}(G)}(t-1).
$$

The source states that this is weaker than the diameter increment conjecture and proves it for graphs of diameter $2$, but gives no general resolution.
literal_record.source_name: David S. Herscovici, Benjamin D. Hester and Glenn H. Hurlbert, “t-Pebbling and Extensions”, arXiv:0905.3949 (2011).
literal_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0905.3949

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2009).

318554.primary_locations_read: 0905.3949 v2 Conjecture 3.7 and surrounding results; v1 differently numbered conjectures and diameter-two theorem
318554.ordinary_attempts: Repeatedly removing a pebble at cost <=2^diam would give the bound, but arbitrary configurations need not permit such a cheap move. The source proves a large-t increment and diameter-two case, not a uniform cheap-extraction lemma. Splitting into t groups of pi(G) gives t*pi(G), which exceeds target whenever pi(G)>2^diam.
318554.precise_gap_or_exclusion: Need configuration-sensitive induction with residual solvability, or graph plus exact worst-root configuration and a nonreachability certificate. Fractional weight inequalities alone do not encode integral reachability.

318555.title: The diameter-three t-pebbling conjecture

literal_record.title: The diameter-three t-pebbling conjecture
literal_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices and diameter $3$, and let $t\geq 1$.

**Diameter-three t-pebbling conjecture.**

$$
\pi_t(G) \leq 1.5n+8t-6.
$$

This follows formally from the linear t-pebbling bound conjecture together with the stated diameter-three bound for ordinary pebbling. The source gives no resolution status.
literal_record.source_name: David S. Herscovici, Benjamin D. Hester and Glenn H. Hurlbert, “t-Pebbling and Extensions”, arXiv:0905.3949 (2011).
literal_record.references:

318839.title: The facet-connectedness conjecture for cutsets

literal_record.title: The facet-connectedness conjecture for cutsets
literal_record.statement: Let $P$ be a polytope, let $F$ be a facet of $P$, and let $C$ be a cutset. **Facet-connectedness conjecture.** The cutset $C$ cannot contain vertices $u$ and $v$ lying in a common facet of $F$ unless there exists a connected path from $u$ to $v$ within $C\cap F$. The source uses this claim in an argument about preserving path lengths under polytope perturbations, but gives no resolution.
literal_record.source_name: Sandeep Koranne and Anand Kulkarni, “Combinatorial Polytope Enumeration”, arXiv:0908.1619 (2009).
literal_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0908.1619

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2009).

318839.primary_locations_read: 0908.1619 definition of realizable cutset, Theorem 3.1 and footnote, Conjecture 6.12 and subsequent purported nonrevisiting proof
318839.ordinary_attempts: For a cutset strictly separated by a linear functional, every nonmaximal vertex of facet F has an improving edge in F. Following improving edges stays on the selected side and ends in the maximizing face, whose graph is connected. This connects every pair in C intersect F, stronger than the claimed common-subfacet condition. This is the source convexity observation plus standard linear-programming edge ascent, a complete classical/source bridge.
318839.precise_gap_or_exclusion: On the realized-cut interpretation excluded as routine, not because short. If cutset instead means arbitrary subset satisfying three combinatorial tests, separation is not supplied; no proof/refutation on that broader reading. Hirsch/nonrevisiting claims in surrounding source cannot be assumed correct. No acceptance.
